items.name: Learning to Trace Seiberg Dualities
items.title: Learning to Trace Seiberg Dualities
items.description: Dualities play an important role in establishing both microscopic and emergent phenomena in a wide range of physical systems. In practice, though, it can often be computationally challenging to establish when two systems are dual, even when all of the "rules of the game" are well-known. Said differently, when confronted with two systems, how can one efficiently establish that they are in fact dual? items.name: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
items.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
items.description: Long visual context poses a challenge for vision-language models: performance degrades as the number of distractors grows, and processing all tokens at once is computationally infeasible under GPU memory constraints. We present ReToken, a single learnable embedding trained as an explicit retrieval target that selects a sparse set of query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache. items.name: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
items.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
items.description: We present PAC-MAN, a perception-aware CBF-RL framework that couples control-barrier safety with deployment-realistic onboard sensing for whole-body humanoid dodgeball. The deployed policy sees the ball only as segmentation-masked depth from a head-mounted camera, while training-time CBF guidance represents clearance to every body link, and an adversarial motion prior regularizes the resulting evasive reflexes. items.name: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
items.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
items.description: Chemistry literature synthesis often requires assembling specific findings scattered across many publications, yet existing literature-search systems primarily return ranked document lists. As a result, scientists and AI agents need to locate relevant information, verify their provenance, and assemble cross-paper answers manually. items.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
items.description: System prompts are instructions configured by developers to govern the behaviors of foundation models in AI applications. They are used throughout commercial AI products, but are rarely disclosed to the public or regulators, creating a serious trust and accountability gap in the wide deployment of AI systems. items.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
items.description: Computer-using agents (CUAs) are advancing rapidly across the digital world. A CUA trajectory records the agent's actions, states, and reasoning. Verifying whether it fulfilled the task instruction is central to CUA evaluation, data curation, and reinforcement learning. items.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
items.description: Clinical risk models routinely achieve strong aggregate performance while producing materially different error rates across patient subgroups. Audit pipelines have been proposed to catch this, but their components are rarely stress-tested, so it is unclear which parts of an audit can be trusted and under what conditions. items.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
items.description: Aligning large language models to prevent them attributing consciousness to themselves inadvertently alters their representations of mindedness in other entities alongside human beliefs and values. items.name: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
items.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
items.description: Scaling coding agents requires a continuing supply of executable data for training, benchmarking, and continuous evaluation. Each task must couple a realistic software state with a specification, development tools, and reliable verification. items.title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
items.description: Multimodal on-policy distillation (OPD) transfers fine-grained visual knowledge by supervising student-generated trajectories with a privileged-view teacher. Yet its next-token corrections are source-mixed, combining visual signals with linguistic priors and teacher-specific effects. items.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
items.description: Post-training quantization (PTQ) has emerged as an effective solution for deploying Vision Transformers (ViTs) on resource-constrained devices. items.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation

items.title: Algorithms for Structured Elections under Thiele Voting Rules

items.title: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
items.description: Deploying autonomous computer-use agents (CUAs) locally is increasingly important for privacy, cost efficiency, and practical usability, yet improving their performance under strict hardware constraints remains challenging. items.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
items.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires AI systems that improve the process of building AI (i.e., AI4AI); machine learning engineering (MLE) offers a concrete, executable testbed for studying this capability. items.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
items.description: Predicting the 3D structures of atomic systems is fundamental to advancing material science and drug discovery. items.name: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
items.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
items.description: Large language models can write, patch, and search code, but oncall root cause analysis (RCA) demands something different: reasoning over noisy metrics, logs, traces, and source code, starting from ambiguous user-facing reports, often hours after the incident began. items.title: ScaFE: Data-Efficient Scar Classification with LLM-Generated Clinical Feature Programs
items.description: Classifying pathological scars from clinical photographs requires distinguishing keloids from hypertrophic scars despite limited expert-labeled data and substantial acquisition variation across hospitals. items.title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields for Spin Dynamics in Metallic Magnets

items.title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
items.description: Large language model-based multi-agent systems improve complex problem solving through task decomposition, agent specialization, information exchange, and intermediate validation. items.title: What to Remove, What to Preserve: Dual-Ambiguity Rectification for All-in-One Image Restoration
items.description: All-in-one image restoration aims to handle diverse degradations within a unified framework. Existing methods commonly encode heterogeneous degradation conditions in a shared latent space, where degradation-related cues and scene content can remain entangled.
